description:
## What

Implement `ZlintBridge::run_on_certs(certs_der: &[&[u8]]) -> Vec<Result<HashMap<String, Verdict>, PerCertError>>` using zlint's multi-file invocation. Amortizes subprocess fork+exec cost across the batch.

Per PKIX-jy95.3: zlint supports `zlint cert1 cert2 cert3 ...` with NDJSON output, one JSON object per cert per line, in input order. zlint does NOT support multi-cert stdin streaming.

## Implementation notes

- Pipeline:
  1. For each input `cert_der`, hash + cache lookup. Collect cache hits; remaining indexes need subprocess.
  2. Write remaining inputs to temp files. Spawn `<zlint_path> -format der <f1> <f2> ...` once. Apply timeout (proportional to batch size? fixed?). Implementation decision: keep `BridgeConfig::timeout` per invocation; document that batch size + timeout interact.
  3. Read stdout as NDJSON. Line N corresponds to input N (the non-cached subset). Parse per line as in `run_on_cert`.
  4. Populate cache for newly-computed entries.
  5. Assemble final `Vec<Result<...>>` in original input order, interleaving cache hits + fresh results.
- Per-cert error handling: if zlint emits an error line for cert N (look for the marker zlint actually emits — verify in implementation), that index's result is `Err(PerCertError::MalformedDer { detail })`. Other certs in the batch are unaffected — per PKIX-jy95.4, per-cert errors do not poison the batch.
- Subprocess-level errors (binary not found, kill, timeout) fail the WHOLE batch — return `Vec<Err(BridgeError-mapped-as-PerCertError)>` or panic the call? Decision: do NOT swallow bridge-level errors as per-cert; surface them through the function signature. Either change return shape to `Result<Vec<Result<..., PerCertError>>, BridgeError>`, or document that callers handle `BridgeError` by checking before calling. Recommend the `Result<Vec<...>, BridgeError>` outer shape — matches `enumerate_lints` and lets callers distinguish bridge failures from per-cert failures cleanly.

## Surface (proposed)

`impl ZlintBridge { pub fn run_on_certs(&self, certs_der: &[&[u8]]) -> Result<Vec<Result<HashMap<String, Verdict>, PerCertError>>, BridgeError>; }`

## Tests

- Integration: 3-cert batch (PKITS certs available locally), one valid + one malformed + one valid. Assert outer `Ok(vec)`, vec length 3, indexes 0 and 2 are `Ok`, index 1 is `Err(MalformedDer)`.
- Cache interaction: run batch twice; second invocation should hit cache entirely (no subprocess; assert via instrumented bridge or by deleting zlint between calls and verifying second call succeeds).
- Empty input: `run_on_certs(&[])` returns `Ok(vec![])` (no subprocess; trivial fast path).
- Single input: `run_on_certs(&[c])` returns same value as `run_on_cert(c)` wrapped in `Ok(vec![Ok(_)])`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `run_on_certs` implementation reusing `run_on_cert`'s cache + parsing primitives
- [ ] Tests: 3-cert batch with malformed-middle, cache equivalence, empty-input, single-input
- [ ] cargo build / clippy --all-features -D warnings / fmt --check / doc --no-deps clean
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased citing PKIX-jy95.7.4

## Out of scope

- Adaptive timeout based on batch size (document interaction, defer adaptation)
- Parallel subprocess spawning for batches > N (yagni; one subprocess for arbitrary-sized batch is the design)

## Cross-references

- PKIX-jy95.7.1 (types)
- PKIX-jy95.7.3 (cache + single-cert primitives this depends on)
- PKIX-jy95.3 (multi-file batch decision)
- PKIX-jy95.4 (per-cert vs bridge-level error discrimination)
title: pkix-zlint-bridge: run_on_certs() batch via multi-file zlint invocation
